title: TrailGuard AI cameras trigger arrest of 39 armed poachers in Similipal Tiger Reserve
summary: AI trail cameras detected armed intruders on 18 Feb 2026; STR Field Director reports 39 surrendered, nine guns seized, case registered.
account: Similipal Tiger Reserve in Mayurbhanj district, Odisha, runs a network of about 220 TrailGuard AI trail cameras that classify humans, animals and vehicles and send images to a control room. Late on Wednesday 18 February 2026 the cameras detected a group of armed intruders entering the reserve; Field Director Prakash Chand Gogineni said the real-time alerts mobilized the Similipal South Division, three ranges and three Special Tiger Protection Force units, and after about 24 hours of combing at least 39 poachers surrendered. Nine guns, gunpowder and more than 20 bows and arrows were recovered and a case was registered at Jenabil Wildlife Range. Later detections on 11 April, around 24 July and 23 September 2026 led to arrests; courts refused bail to the July and September groups. The camera count varies by source: the Field Director gave 'around 220' in February 2026 and The Hans India 'over 220' in July 2026, while the Times of India in April 2026 reported 50 AI cameras in use, up from an initial 10, with 300 planned.
purpose: Detect human intruders and poachers entering the reserve in near real time so rangers can intercept them before wildlife is killed.
system: TrailGuard AI camera network (about 220 units) with embedded human/animal/vehicle classification
deployer: Similipal Tiger Reserve, Odisha Forest Department (Similipal South Division, Special Tiger Protection Force, Similipal Wildlife Intelligence Network)
taxonomy_note: Closest fit; the direct benefit is wildlife-law enforcement (interception and prosecution of armed poachers) rather than sustainability in a narrow sense.

ratings.reason: Unassessed: no specific injury to rangers avoided is documented; the reports describe arrests and seizures.
The reserve's Field Director states the detection and 24-hour operation averted a major poaching incident and yielded nine guns and 20-plus bows and arrows.
Repeated interceptions of armed groups inside a tiger reserve, with nine guns and more than 20 bows and arrows seized, are material to the reserve's wildlife.

ai_role.statement: The AI cameras' real-time detection of the armed group is the stated trigger for the mobilization that ended in surrender and seizure; the park authority's statement is the Field Director's on-record account quoted by The New Indian Express and the Times of India, and court remands are press-reported (PTI, Hans India, Ommcom). No official press note or court order could be fetched, so this resubmission rests on press-quoted forest-department statements.
